coverage: All seven constant-pace controls checked against independent closed-form work, fatigue, energy, outcome and dose calculations.
Analytic high-to-low pace switch checks fatigue recovery and accumulated work; late acceleration checks exact full-work clipping and fatigue stopping at completion.
Exact win/pass thresholds and distinguishable values just below each threshold; terminal states remain immutable.
80 seeded switching histories with independently sampled midpoint numerical oracles, using 0.002 simulated-minute steps.
Randomized solar output, transmission, habitat load, battery capacity and initial energy; repeated histories compared across random frame partitions.
Stored-energy conservation including unserved load and curtailed generation; exact empty-then-charging and capacity-clipping fixtures.
Half-speed and double-speed comfort clocks preserve simulated outcomes; microsecond frame increments preserve progress.
Every full default round ends with automatic shelter entry at 1800 simulated seconds and the same 10.9375 microgray integrated authored dose.
limitations: Fatigue coefficients and the rising radiation profile are authored lesson assumptions, not validated astronaut physiology or live NASA radiation observations.
The 210 microgray/day historical reference is converted using 86,400 seconds; this audit checks the implemented mathematics, not a new measurement or primary-source validation.
No medical inference, microgray-to-sievert conversion, dose bonus, hardware validation or learning-outcome claim follows from these tests.

Randomized coverage is finite. The independent numerical oracle allows 0.00015 fatigue and 0.00002 work/energy/dose absolute error for finite-step clipping; closed-form and frame-partition checks use much tighter tolerances.
The numerical oracle varies electrical parameters and control histories while keeping default fatigue coefficients, four-section work capacity and 30-minute duration.
